unit-m5u3.title: Unit 5 · Lesson 3: Divide with Area Models and Properties
unit-m5u3.source: enVision Topic 5 Student Edition practice pages — dividing by two-digit divisors (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 5-3 practice pages: using area models, place value and the Distributive Property to divide by two-digit divisors, and multiplying to check.

why.text: The area model shows WHY division works in tens and ones. Partial quotients and long division, next in the unit, are this same model written in a column.

objectives.text: Use an area model to divide by a two-digit divisor
Use the Distributive Property to break a quotient into tens and ones
Use a quotient to answer a word problem's real question

parentNote.text: Built from the lesson 5-3 practice pages in her Unit 5 folder, read for what they ask. The numbers are fresh, not the page's own. The slip most worth a word is writing the two parts of the side next to each other (20 and 8 as 208 instead of 28); one question shows a student doing exactly that. The other wrong options stop after the tens piece or count one group too many. One question shows a check that is right, because a good critique says so when an answer holds up.

nextUp.text: Tens first, then what is left, then add the parts and multiply back.

cards.def:
**A rectangle shows a division: the area is the dividend, one side is the divisor, and the missing side is the quotient.**
• 476 ÷ 14: area 476, side 14, missing side 34.

**To find a missing side, divide the area by the side you know.**
• 14 × w = 476, so w = 476 ÷ 14.

**Estimate how many tens are in the quotient before anything else.**
• 312 ÷ 13: 13 × 20 = 260 fits, 13 × 30 = 390 does not, so 2 tens.
cards.hint: The biggest ten that still fits.

cards.def:
**Subtract the first piece, then find how many more groups fit.**
• 312 − 260 = 52, and 13 × 4 = 52, so 4 more.
cards.hint: Take away, then share what remains.

cards.def:
**Split the missing side into tens and ones, and the pieces of area add back to the whole.**
• 364 = 14 × 20 + 14 × 6 = 14 × (20 + 6), so 364 ÷ 14 = 26.

cards.term: Add the parts, never side by side
cards.def:
**The quotient is the tens part PLUS the ones part.**
• 20 and 8 make 28, not 208.

**Divisor × quotient should give back the area.**
• 18 × 31 = 540 + 18 = 558.

**In a word problem, the quotient is often a step, not the answer.**
• Find the width, then decide whether it fits the space.
cards.hint: Read the question again before you write the answer.

questions.q: A rectangle has an area of 476 square inches. One side is 14 inches long. Which equation finds the other side, w?
questions.hint: Area = length × width. Which operation undoes the multiplying?
steps: To find a missing factor, divide.

ex.main: **476 ÷ 14 = w.** A missing side is the area divided by the side you know. Here w = 34.
ex.tip: Dividing the smaller number by the bigger one gives less than 1, which cannot be the side.

questions.q: In an area model for 476 ÷ 14, what does the missing side stand for?
questions.hint: The area is 476, and one side is 14.
steps: The whole area is the dividend, 476.
The side you know is the divisor, 14.
The side you are finding is the quotient.

ex.main: **The quotient.** Area ÷ known side = missing side, so the missing side is the answer to the division: 34.
ex.tip: Dividend = area, divisor = known side, quotient = missing side.

questions.q: What is the best first step for finding 312 ÷ 13 with an area model?
opts: Add 312 and 13 to find the area of the whole rectangle first
Find the ones first: 13 × 2 = 26, so the answer must be 2
Find the tens: 13 × 20 = 260 fits, and 13 × 30 = 390 is too much
Divide 13 by 312 to find how wide the first piece should be
questions.hint: Start by estimating how many tens will be in the quotient.

ex.main: **Find the tens first.** 13 × 20 = 260 fits and 13 × 30 = 390 does not, so the first piece of the side is 20.
ex.tip: Tens first, then the ones with what is left.

steps: Estimate the tens: 17 × 20 = 340, and 17 × 30 = 510 is too much.
Add the two parts of the side: 20 + 2 = 22.

ex.main: **22.** The side is 20 + 2 = 22, and 17 × 22 = 374. The wrong answers are real slips: 20 is only the tens piece, 202 writes 20 and 2 side by side, and 23 is one group too many.
ex.tip: Add the parts of the side; never write them side by side.

steps: Estimate the tens: 29 × 20 = 580, and 29 × 30 = 870 is too much.
Add the two parts of the side: 20 + 4 = 24.

ex.main: **24.** The side is 20 + 4 = 24, and 29 × 24 = 696. The wrong answers are real slips: 20 is only the tens piece, 204 writes 20 and 4 side by side, and 25 is one group too many.

questions.q: Which shows 364 ÷ 14 using the Distributive Property?
questions.hint: Split the missing side into tens and ones. Do the pieces add back to 364?

ex.main: **14 × 20 + 14 × 6 = 14 × (20 + 6) = 364.** The two pieces add back to 364, so the quotient is 26.
ex.tip: Check that the pieces add back to the whole: 14 × 2 + 14 × 6 is only 112.

questions.q: A rectangular rug has an area of 432 square feet. One side is 18 feet. How many feet long is the other side?
steps: Estimate the tens: 18 × 20 = 360, and 18 × 30 = 540 is too much.
Add the two parts of the side: 20 + 4 = 24.

ex.main: **24 feet.** The side is 20 + 4 = 24, and 18 × 24 = 432. The wrong answers are real slips: 20 feet is only the tens piece, 204 feet writes 20 and 4 side by side, and 25 feet is one group too many.

questions.q: A choir of 351 singers stands in 13 equal rows. How many singers are in each row?
steps: Estimate the tens: 13 × 20 = 260, and 13 × 30 = 390 is too much.
Add the two parts of the side: 20 + 7 = 27.

ex.main: **27 singers.** The side is 20 + 7 = 27, and 13 × 27 = 351. The wrong answers are real slips: 20 singers is only the tens piece, 207 singers writes 20 and 7 side by side, and 28 singers is one group too many.
ex.tip: Check: 13 rows × your answer must make 351.

questions.q: In an area model for 575 ÷ 23, the first piece is 23 × 20 = 460. Which multiplication fills the second piece?
questions.hint: How much of 575 is left after the first piece?

ex.tip: Every piece of the model uses the same side, 23.

questions.q: How many tens will be in the quotient of 816 ÷ 34?

ex.main: **2 tens.** 34 × 20 fits under 816 but 34 × 30 goes over, so the quotient is in the twenties: 24.
ex.tip: Estimating the tens first stops you from starting with a piece that is too big.

questions.q: Jada found 558 ÷ 18 = 31. Which multiplication checks her answer?
questions.hint: Multiply the quotient by the divisor.

ex.main: **18 × 31 = 540 + 18 = 558.** Quotient × divisor gives back the dividend, so her answer checks out.
ex.tip: 18 × 3 forgets that the 3 in 31 means 3 tens.

questions.q: Noah used an area model for 448 ÷ 16. His pieces were 16 × 20 = 320 and 16 × 8 = 128, and he wrote the answer 208. What went wrong?
opts: He should multiply 20 and 8 to get 160, the real side length
His first piece was wrong, because 16 × 20 is really 300
Nothing went wrong, because 208 is the correct quotient here
He wrote 20 and 8 side by side; he should add them to get 28
steps: Writing 20 and 8 side by side makes 208, which is far too big.

ex.main: **He wrote the parts side by side.** The side is 20 + 8 = 28, and 16 × 28 = 448. 16 × 208 would be 3,328.
ex.tip: Add the parts of the side together, the same way you add partial products.

questions.q: Priya says 667 ÷ 29 = 23. She checks: 29 × 20 = 580 and 29 × 3 = 87, and 580 + 87 = 667. Is she right?
opts: Yes, because the two pieces add back to 667
No, because 29 × 3 is 97, so the answer is 24
No, because 667 is odd, so it cannot be divided by 29
Yes, but only because 23 is close to 20

ex.main: **Yes.** Both pieces are right and they add back to 667, so 23 is the quotient.
ex.tip: A good check says so when an answer is right, too.

questions.q: A garden bed has an area of 672 square feet and is 28 feet long. Will it fit in a space that is 25 feet wide?
opts: No, because it is 26 feet wide
Yes, because it is 24 feet wide
Yes, because it is 20 feet wide
steps: 24 feet is less than 25, so it fits.

ex.main: **Yes, it is 24 feet wide.** 28 × 24 = 672, and 24 feet fits in a 25-foot space with 1 foot to spare.
ex.tip: Answer the question that was asked: the width is a step, "will it fit" is the answer.

questions.q: A train travels 45 miles each hour. How many hours will it take to go 630 miles?
steps: Estimate the tens: 45 × 10 = 450, and 45 × 20 = 900 is too much.
Add the two parts of the side: 10 + 4 = 14.

ex.main: **14 hours.** The side is 10 + 4 = 14, and 45 × 14 = 630. The wrong answers are real slips: 10 hours is only the tens piece, 104 hours writes 10 and 4 side by side, and 15 hours is one group too many.
ex.tip: Check: 45 miles × your answer must make 630.
